decisive_semantics.reference_output_parameters: bb is the dying block (read-only); outblock = bb->getOut(0) and outblock_ind = bb->getOutRevIndex(0) anchor the dead edge; origvn/replacevn are Varnode references where replacevn is freshly created (newUnique under neednewunique, else newVarnode at origvn address) and canonicalized through VarnodeBank::setDef in opSetOutput; the artificial MULTIEQUAL replaceop enters outblock via opInsertBegin.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_traversal_order: bb ops iterate in block order; the descendant scan walks the descend list in insertion order with the inner slot scan bounded by numInput() skipping i==outblock_ind; the branch construction walks i<outblock->sizeIn() in in-edge order; the rewrite loop starts at descend.begin() AFTER opInsertBegin so the artificial phi trails the list and is skipped by the dead-edge guard, exactly as funcdata_block.cc:106-169.
decisive_semantics.counter_accumulator_lifecycle: needreplace and neednewunique reset to false once per origop (cc:104-105); deadEdge resets to true once per scanned descendant (cc:109); no accumulation crosses phi boundaries.
decisive_semantics.sorting_comparison_keys: All identity comparisons are pointer equality (op, varnode, block); address equality is consulted only for neednewunique (origvn addr == out-block MULTIEQUAL output addr AND isAddrTied, the addrtied|insert dual flag of varnode.hh:250); branch selection key is outblock->getIn(i) == bb.

analysis_options.funcdata: Three isolated function shells (BfdArchitecture over 40a32358:examples/curl on the oracle side; fresh bare Funcdata on the Rugra side). No followFlow and no Action pass; six synthetic BlockBasics per case.
analysis_options.placeholder_construction: Each case builds p1,p2 -> m -> o <- a -> d with o in[0]=m and in[1]=a; m holds a 2-input MULTIEQUAL origphi with output origvn at 0x2000; o holds a MULTIEQUAL ophi reading origvn at slot 0 (the dead edge) and a RAM varnode w at slot 1; case reader_beyond/addrtied_unique add a COPY reader of origvn in d. Outputs use the newVarnode+opSetOutput idiom (the same idiom pushMultiequals uses for replacevn) so the space assignment is identical on both sides.
analysis_options.case_matrix: needreplace true/false crossed with neednewunique false/true; the dead-edge guard and the post-construction descend-rewrite order are observed through op order, input slots, descend list and bank counts
analysis_options.diagnostics: BfdArchitecture initialization diagnostics captured privately and excluded from the target API observation
analysis_options.normalization: Stable vN encounter labels over first-appearance order (outputs then inputs) across [m,o,d] ops preserve all aliasing; opcode, SeqNum time, Varnode create index, size, space index, constant flag, offset, origvn descend list as (block,slot) pairs and alive/dead/varnode counts are byte-compared. The environment-dependent addrtied marking produced by the real-function local-scope query on the oracle side is input-side fixture state, not an output of pushMultiequals, and is excluded from the projection; the addrtied branch itself stays observable through the unique-space replacement varnode (sp2/x0x10000000) in addrtied_unique.
